evidence.quote: The South Fork Payette River drains about 1,200 square miles (3,100 km2), originating on the west side of the Sawtooth Wilderness beneath the 10,211-foot (3,112 m) Mount Payette. It flows past Grandjean and down to Lowman, along Highway 21.

evidence.claim: The improved roadway has informational and rafting pullouts and carries tourists, rafters and commuters.
evidence.quote: Now it is a fully modern paved roadway with informational and white water rafting pull-outs, which serves to transport tourists, rafters, commuters, and other traffic across the middle Idaho region.

evidence.quote: The "Main" run of the Payette River begins at Banks and parallels Highway 55 down to Horseshoe Bend, while the "Staircase" run on the South Fork ends at Banks.

evidence.quote: The city was founded in 1934, and then incorporated as a city in 1951 to bring legal alcohol and gambling to the area.

evidence.claim: Natural hot springs reach the surface in the middle of Lowman and elsewhere in the surrounding mountains.

evidence.claim: The community takes its name from Nathaniel Winfield Lowman, an Iowa homesteader who settled here in 1907.
evidence.quote: The community was named for a homesteader, Nathaniel Winfield Lowman, from Polk County, Iowa, who settled there in 1907.

evidence.claim: In 1989, wildfire burned more than 45,000 acres in the Lowman area and destroyed 26 structures, without injuries or deaths.

evidence.claim: Lowman stands on the north bank of the South Fork in central Idaho, at 3,960 feet above sea level.
evidence.quote: along the north bank of the South Fork of the Payette River in the central part of the state, at an elevation of 3,960 feet (1,210 m) above sea level.

flags: The Crouch cache places road-improvement discussion after a 2018 business inventory without a clear construction date. The story states the documented change without assigning a year, builder or motive.
Dropped current claim that the main road passes through Crouch; the cache does not establish that alignment. Retained Crouch as the existing town moment in the supplied strip order.
Visit Idaho gives 35.8 miles; Lowman text gives 33 and catalog mapping 33.3. The overview explicitly uses the tourism office’s length and estimated time.

Crouch incorporation purpose and Lowman’s active one-room school rely on cached secondary accounts. No access to the school or hot springs is promised. The current national count of schools is supported in the cache but omitted as unnecessary precision.
No original road-level motifs were supplied; an empty array is used.
